theory.overview: The Union-Find (Disjoint Set Union - DSU) data structure manages a collection of disjoint sets. It supports two main operations: Find (determine which set an element belongs to) and Union (merge two sets). With path compression and union by rank/size, both operations achieve nearly constant O(α(n)) amortized time, where α is the inverse Ackermann function (practically < 5). Essential for Kruskal's algorithm, cycle detection, and connected components.

keyConcepts.name: Path Compression
keyConcepts.description: During Find, flatten the structure by making every node point directly to root. Dramatically speeds up future queries.

keyConcepts.name: Union by Rank/Size
keyConcepts.description: Always attach smaller tree under larger tree root. Keeps tree shallow, ensuring O(log n) without compression.

keyConcepts.name: Inverse Ackermann
keyConcepts.description: α(n) grows extremely slowly. For all practical n (up to 10^600), α(n) < 5. Effectively constant time.

keyConcepts.name: Applications
keyConcepts.description: Kruskal's MST, cycle detection in undirected graphs, connected components, image processing, least common ancestor.

algorithmSteps.description: Initialize 5 sets. Each element is its own parent, rank = 0.
Union(0, 1): Same rank, attach 1 to 0. New rank of 0 = 1.
Union(2, 3): Same rank, attach 3 to 2. New rank of 2 = 1.
Find(3): Path compression. 3's parent is 2 (already root).
Union(0's set, 2's set): Rank equal, attach 2 to 0. Root 0 now rank 2.
Find(3): Path compression! 3 now points directly to root 0.
